name: Rover safety bicycle
description: A low-wheeled, chain-driven bicycle expanded the range of designs for individual land transport.

impact.note: Made cycling usable by ordinary riders across many societies and set the lasting bicycle form; later bicycles are direct refinements of it.

places.note: Modern country or regional reference; historic political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: John Kemp Starley’s 1885 Rover was a low-wheeled, chain-driven safety bicycle.
events.caveats: An earlier chain-driven safety design by Lawson appeared in 1879; no unique invention or sales count is asserted.

evidence.supports: Smithsonian history identifies the Rover model and year.
Museum history identifies Starley with the 1885 model.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event sourced for this particular record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The source describes several earlier safety bicycles; the 1885 Rover is a specific documented configuration.

research.note: Initial sourced admission; classification and interpretations await independent review.
